Welcome. This is a catalogue-driven BSS proof of concept on Google Cloud, patterned on TM Forum. In three minutes: how a product manager launches a mobile plan, how commercial rules are configured, and how each order is decomposed into a network-ready service order.

It starts with a reusable library. Ten product specifications, from mobile access and UK voice to roaming, voicemail and data gifting, realize into seven customer-facing service specifications. Reuse is deliberate: UK voice and international calling share the Mobile Voice CFS with separate buckets, and roaming amends the existing Mobile Line instead of creating a new service.

Service designers own the realization: CFS dependencies, cardinality and instance keys. Voicemail requires Mobile Voice, which requires exactly one primary Mobile Line. Instances are keyed by subscription and line, so overlapping products merge into one service rather than duplicating it.

That makes go-to-market simple. The product manager picks specifications, sets allowances and price, in the studio or by describing the plan to Gemini. The platform generates the product offering, the composite product specification and the inherited CFS realization. The product manager never touches service design.

Publication is gated. An offering moves from Draft to Active only when every leaf specification has a CFS mapping with matching units. Retiring an offer stops new sales, while existing orders keep their snapshots.

Commercial rules are configurable lookup tables: eligibility, price, discount and approval. A rule can be typed or spoken in plain English. Gemini drafts the row, and the rules engine validates it before anyone saves. Need a new input, like contract length? It becomes a new column. The highest priority wins, ties are rejected, and effective dates apply. No code, no redeploy.

Configure, price, quote. CPQ qualifies the customer segment, applies term prices and product constraints, such as one primary plan and add-ons needing a parent, and applies dated promotions. The quote is TMF648-shaped, valid for thirty days, and pins the catalogue and rule versions used.

The AI channel follows the same guardrails. Gemini only proposes active offering IDs; it never sets prices or allowances. Deterministic code validates the proposal, and any discount or exception is held for a human.
On acceptance, a TMF622 ProductOrder is generated from the stored quote and validated against it, so tampered or stale payloads are rejected, and resubmission is idempotent.

Then decomposition. Each ordered composite resolves to its leaf specifications and their CFSs, producing a TMF641-shaped service order: voice minutes for the HSS, data allowance for the packet gateway profile, and SMS for the SMSC, with characteristics carried across.

That service order is the hand-off to service order management, the TMFC007 pattern, which drives resource orders and activation adapters toward the network elements. Those adapters are the next integration step; today nothing is provisioned. That's the flow: reusable specifications, configurable rules, and a network-ready order.
